source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Explain that exercise is the only predictable asthma trigger, so viral infections, smoke, cold air, and allergens do not need consideration.","B":"Explain that asthma triggers may include respiratory infections, smoke or poor air quality, cold air, exercise, and relevant allergens, with individual variation.","C":"Explain that environmental triggers stop influencing asthma after controller therapy is prescribed, making exposure assessment unnecessary.","D":"Explain that asthma exacerbations occur independently of recognizable exposures, so identifying individual triggers does not help management."}}
source_row.rationale: NHLBI lists allergens, exercise, respiratory infections, poor air quality, cold air and other exposures among asthma triggers; trigger patterns differ among individuals.

source_row.stem: A client with asthma asks which exposures can trigger symptoms. Which response is accurate?
